instructions.title: File Format Instructions
instructions.columnsBody: Each column header is the key of the document it fills. A document's key is shown next to it in Data Management → Works & Documents. Headers are matched to keys case-insensitively.
instructions.noKeyYet: — no key set yet; set one in Works & Documents
instructions.passageKey: passage_key — optional; the shared identity for a row across every document
instructions.metadata: {{example}} — optional; the page in that document's printed source. Any column named document key + .field is stored as paragraph metadata.
instructions.xlsxNote: An XLSX file works the same way — put the document keys in the first (header) row.
instructions.matchingSubset: Include any subset of the documents — one column or all of them. A new reference can be added later as a single column.
instructions.matchingAlign: Rows are aligned to existing data by passage key and/or position, which must be consistent with what's already stored. Add a passage_key column to target specific passages regardless of row order.
instructions.matchingUpsert: The import is a pure upsert: matching rows are updated, new rows inserted, and existing rows not in the file are left unchanged — nothing is deleted. So only the rows that need changing need to be included.
instructions.matchingEmptyCells: Empty cells are skipped; a column that is entirely empty (or absent) leaves that document untouched.
instructions.matchingMetadata: Metadata columns work differently: a filled cell sets the field, an empty cell clears it, and a field with no column is left alone. A row with metadata but no text updates the paragraph already there.
instructions.setupSection: Each document's section (matched to this section by order) must already exist and be named.
instructions.setupSkipped: Reference columns whose key isn't a reference on this project, or whose section isn't set up, are skipped and reported after import.

warning.title: Not a routine task
warning.routine: Everyday edits, imports and deletes keep the paragraph search index up to date on their own. You should rarely need this page.
warning.when: Rebuild only when the index has drifted from the database:
warning.whenOutside: after bulk changes made outside the app — seeding, hand-written SQL, restoring a backup;
warning.whenSyncFailed: after an import reported that the search sync failed;
warning.whenCodeChanged: after a code change to what a search record holds, or to the settings below.
warning.editing: The new index replaces the old one in a single swap, so search keeps working and never shows a half-built index. But a paragraph saved while the rebuild runs can be missed: run it when nobody is editing, or run it again afterwards.
warning.script: The same rebuild can be run from a terminal:

report.title: Paragraph index
report.description: What a rebuild would do now. Nothing has been written; the figures are read fresh each time this page loads. Only counts and settings are compared, not the records' contents, so a matching index can still hold out-of-date records — after a change to the record shape, rebuild anyway.

settings.title: Search settings
settings.description: How the index searches. These are defined in code and applied by every rebuild, so changes made in the Algolia dashboard are overwritten. To change one, change it in

help.searchableAttributes: Only the paragraph text is searched, never ids.
help.typoTolerance: Results with typos appear only when nothing matches with fewer. Keeps English results precise; a misspelled query finds less.
help.advancedSyntax: A "quoted phrase" must match as a phrase, and -word leaves out results containing that word.
